en: The Chapter on Non-Proliferation, Concerning the Question on Inference.
8. Questions on the Indivisible Training Rules (Anavasesa-sikkhāpada) “Venerable Nāgasena, those who were the former teachers of physicians—
namely, Nārada, Dhammantari, Aṅgirasa, Kapila, Kaṇḍaraggi, Sāma, Atula, and Pubbakaccāyana— all these...”

The teachers, having known all that without exception—the arising of diseases, their causes, their essential natures, their origins, their treatments, their procedures, and their success or failure—grasped them all at once in a single bundle, thinking, "In this body, so many diseases will arise," and bound them together in a sutra; yet they were not omniscient. Why?
However, although the Tathāgata is omniscient, having known future actions through his Buddha-knowledge,
he did not lay down the training rules in their entirety by delimiting them beforehand— thinking, "In such-and-such a matter,
such-and-such a training rule must be laid down"— but rather as each matter arose, when infamy became manifest and faults were widespread and manifold.
“Did the Tathāgata prescribe the training rules for his disciples at various times when people were complaining?
“It is known, Great King, by the Tathāgata: ‘At this time, among these people, more than one hundred and fifty training rules will have to be prescribed.
Moreover, it occurred to the Tathāgata: ‘If indeed I—”
"I shall prescribe one hundred and fifty training rules all at once; the great multitude will fall into terror, thinking, 'Much must be guarded here;
it is indeed difficult to go forth in the teaching of the ascetic Gotama!
Those who desire to go forth will not go forth, and they will not have faith in my words. Lacking faith, those people will be destined for the states of misery."
"In whatever matters may arise in the future, having made the teaching of the Dhamma understood and the faults manifest, we shall lay down the training rule.
"It is wonderful, venerable Nāgasena! It is marvelous, venerable Nāgasena!
How great is the omniscient knowledge of the Tathāgata! It is even so, venerable Nāgasena; this has been well demonstrated."

“There is a reason why the Tathāgata [did not teach all training rules at once]: if beings were to hear that ‘much must be trained in here,’ terror might arise in them, and not even a single person would go forth in the Conqueror’s dispensation; I accept it as being exactly so.
This is the eighth question on the training rules without remainder.
